Hi Arielle — thanks for the note and the MAP template. We can support a dual-path MAP that should address procurement concerns while keeping the pilot timeline tight. High-level proposal below; happy to refine during a quick call.

Overview (dual-path approach):

Path A — Standard onramp (preferred)
- Preconditions: countersigned Order Form + executed DPA
- Evidence window: 30 days for core SOC2 items (required), optional integrations follow on 60-day cadence
- Timeline to pilot: ~4–6 weeks after order form execution (assuming legal turnaround of 7–10 business days)

Path B — Staged onramp with provisional access (procurement-friendly)
- Preconditions: countersigned provisional Order Form + PO + escrow agreement for critical keys/configuration
- Legal sequencing: MSA/DPA redlines continue in parallel; provisional license expires or transitions to full license on contract execution or at end of escrow period
- Evidence window: same 30/60 split; we log all evidence and flag missing items to avoid scope creep
- Timeline to pilot: can potentially start within 2–3 weeks of provisional order form/PO if escrow ops are agreed

Next steps I suggest:
1) Internal alignment call between Redwood legal and your procurement to confirm acceptable escrow language and provisional order form template (30–45 minute call)
2) Redwood sends a one-page provisional order form + escrow terms (we can reuse a standard clause)
3) Helio confirms whether Path A or Path B preferred; roadmap timeline updated in MAP

I can get a provisional order form and an internal legal note on sequencing to you by EOD tomorrow. Attaching a short response doc with the proposed sequencing for your records.

Attachment (for tracking): Redwood_MAP_response.pdf (PDF)

Thanks — looping Laura and Karthik for legal & procurement sequencing input.

—Jonas

All — quick legal note on sequencing and risks so we can present a crisp path to Helio. Below are recommended guardrails for Path B (provisional access) to limit risk and keep procurement happy.

Key legal guardrails (recommended):
- Provisional order form must include: explicit term limit (e.g., 60 days), clear statement that provisional access is not an admission of liability, and an escrow release trigger tied to executed DPA/MSA or a mutually agreed remediation plan.
- Technical controls: provisional keys should be scoped and auditable (read-only or limited ingest rate), and logging must be enabled with retention aligning to the DPA evidence requirements.
- Evidence pipeline: create a shared evidence tracker (sheet) listing required SOC2 artifacts; Helio provides core items within 10 business days of provisional start to prevent gating later acceptance.
- Escape hatch: if evidence does not meet minimum within 30 days, we step down capacity and move to sandbox-only until requirements met.

Order form processing note:
- Order form countersignature can be used to provision billing/PO processing, but we should avoid revenue recognition or irreversible provisioning until the DPA is executed; provisional billing can be agreed at a discounted trial rate and invoiced separately.

I will draft the provisional order form language and a short redline matrix for Helio by EOD tomorrow. Jonas — please confirm the technical scoping you want in the provisional keys (rate limits / ingest caps).

Irene Choi
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Irene / Laura — thanks, this is exactly the kind of clarity procurement wanted. We discussed internally and Helio is willing to proceed on Path B (staged onramp + provisional order form) provided we agree to the guardrails below:

Agreed items requested by Helio:

- Ingest cap: 50k tokens/day during provisional period; provisioning to full capacity only after DPA executed
- Logging: Redwood to provide access to evidence tracker and initial SOC2 artifacts (see attachment) within 7 business days of provisional start
- Billing: provisional access billed at a trial rate; final billing adjustments made upon full contract execution
